'''Vitaly Bergelson''' (born 1950 in [[Kiev]]<ref name="mc"/>) is a mathematical researcher and professor at [[Ohio State University]]<!--Wikipedians do not use "The" as part of Ohio State's name; it is considered a marketing gimmick, and routinely deleted.--> in [[Columbus, Ohio]].  His research focuses on [[ergodic theory]] and [[combinatorics]].

Bergelson received his Ph.D. in 1984 under [[Hillel Furstenberg]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name="mc"/>
He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited address at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2006 in Madrid.<ref>{{cite book | last=Bergelson | first=Vitaly | chapter=Ergodic Ramsey theory: a dynamical approach to static theorems | title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Madrid, Spain, August 2006, Volume II, Invited Lectures| date=2007 | doi=10.4171/022-2/79 | doi-access=free | url=http://www.math.ohio-state.edu/~vitaly/Madrid.pdf | access-date=2025-08-06 | page=1655–1678}}</ref>
Among Bergelson's best known results is a polynomial generalization of [[Szemerédi's theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Szemerédi | first=E. | author-link=Endre Szemerédi| title=On sets of integers containing k elements in arithmetic progression | journal=Acta Arithmetica | volume=27 | issue=1 | date=1975 | issn=0065-1036 | pages=199–245 | url=https://eudml.org/doc/205339 | access-date=2025-08-06}}Collection of articles in memory of Juriĭ Vladimirovič Linnik.</ref> The latter provided a positive solution to the famous Erdős–Turán conjecture from 1936 stating that any set of integers of positive upper density contains arbitrarily long [[arithmetic progression]]s. In a 1996 paper Bergelson and Leibman obtained an analogous statement for "polynomial progressions".<ref>{{cite journal | last=Bergelson | first=V. | last2=Leibman | first2=A. | title=Polynomial extensions of van der Waerden’s and Szemerédi’s theorems | journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society | publisher=American Mathematical Society (AMS) | volume=9 | issue=3 | year=1996 | issn=0894-0347 | doi=10.1090/s0894-0347-96-00194-4 | doi-access=free | pages=725–753 | url=https://www.ams.org/jams/1996-9-03/S0894-0347-96-00194-4/S0894-0347-96-00194-4.pdf | access-date=2025-08-06}}</ref>  The Bergelson-Leibman theorem<ref name="mc">{{cite book | last=Soifer | first=Alexander | others=Forewords by Branko Grünbaum, Peter D. Johnson Jr., and Cecil C. Rousseau | title=The Mathematical Coloring Book: Mathematics of Coloring and the Colorful Life of Its Creators | publisher=Springer | publication-place=New York | date=2008 | isbn=0-387-74640-4 | page=358 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vn3GLf-4YkEC&dq=%22Vitali+Bergelson%22&pg=PA358 }}</ref> and the techniques developed in its proof spurred significant further applications and generalizations, particularly in the recent work of [[Terence Tao]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Tao | first=Terence | title=A Quantitative Ergodic Theory Proof of Szemerédi's Theorem | journal=The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics | volume=13 | issue=1 | date=2006 | issn=1077-8926 | doi=10.37236/1125 | doi-access=free | url=https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v13i1r99/pdf | access-date=2025-08-06 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Tao | first=Terence | author-link=Terence Tao| last2=Ziegler | first2=Tamar |author2-link=Tamar Ziegler | title=The primes contain arbitrarily long polynomial progressions | journal=Acta Mathematica | volume=201 | issue=2 | date=2008 | issn=0001-5962 | doi=10.1007/s11511-008-0032-5 | doi-access=free | pages=213–305 | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/acta-mathematica/volume-201/issue-2/The-primes-contain-arbitrarily-long-polynomial-progressions/10.1007/s11511-008-0032-5.pdf | access-date=2025-08-06}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
